l: King Rinkitink, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Rinkitink recognizes the approaching fleet as belonging to his people of Gilgad and fears being forced to return to rule. He agrees to leave after three days of feasting with King Kitticut, then departs for Gilgad with Prince Bobo and sings a farewell song.

l: King Kitticut, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: King Kitticut listens to Rinkitink's protests and tells him that it is his duty to reign because fate made him a king. Although he will grieve their separation, he accepts that Rinkitink must return to Gilgad.

l: Prince Inga, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Prince Inga joins the watchers when the fleet approaches. Rinkitink asks him to get his pearls so they can protect him from the people of Gilgad.

l: Prince Bobo of Boboland, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Prince Bobo laughs when Rinkitink is found and says that Rinkitink has been caught and will be obliged to reign again. He decides to accompany Rinkitink rather than desert his former master and present friend.

l: Lord High Chancellor, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Lord Pinkerbloo kneels before Rinkitink and announces that the people of Gilgad have found their king. He insists that Rinkitink must return home to rule, explaining that the people searched many islands and could not appoint a new king while he might still be alive.

l: the people of Gilgad, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The people of Gilgad have been in despair since Rinkitink disappeared and join the search for him. After finding him at Pingaree, they celebrate his return and escort him home in their decorated boats.

l: Pingaree, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Pingaree receives the people of Gilgad and hosts three days of extraordinary feasting and merriment before Rinkitink leaves. Its people give Rinkitink a royal farewell from the shore.

l: Gilgad, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Gilgad is Rinkitink's kingdom and the place to which his people insist he return. Rinkitink is expected to resume ruling there.

l: fleet of boats, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: A fleet of fifty beautifully decorated boats approaches Pingaree from the south. The boats carry Gilgad's people and include a splendid vessel with a golden throne and Rinkitink's royal robe.

l: search for Rinkitink, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: The people of Gilgad search for Rinkitink throughout many islands of the Nonestic Ocean after he mysteriously disappears. They eventually search Pingaree because it is the source of precious pearls and find him there.

l: festival in Pingaree, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: After Rinkitink agrees to return to Gilgad, Pingaree holds three days of feasting and jollity. Rinkitink makes the most of the celebration, and everyone laughs and sings with him by day and night.

l: Rinkitink's departure for Gilgad, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Rinkitink's departure takes place after three days of celebration. He is escorted in a grand procession to his boat, seated on a golden throne, and sent away by the people of Pingaree while Prince Bobo accompanies him.

l: Rinkitink's duty to reign, Rinkitink in Oz, Chapter Twenty-Four
s: Rinkitink's subjects and King Kitticut maintain that he must return to rule because he was born to be their king. Rinkitink dislikes the duties and ceremonies of kingship, but agrees that there is no honorable escape from this responsibility.

l: Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The document is a fantasy adventure centered on two converging quests: Queen Ann Soforth of Oogaboo’s comic attempt to conquer the world and Shaggy Man’s effort to rescue his lost brother, the Ugly One, from Ruggedo, the Nome King. Ann raises Oogaboo’s eighteen men into an overranked army, with Jo Files as its sole Private, and marches toward Oz; Glinda secretly diverts them away from Oz. Meanwhile, Betsy Bobbin and her mule Hank survive a shipwreck, are expelled from the Rose Kingdom with Shaggy Man and Princess Ozga, and join Polychrome and Tik-Tok in searching for Shaggy’s imprisoned brother. The two parties meet when Ann tries to conquer the travelers. Hank scatters her soldiers, and Shaggy’s Love Magnet makes them friends. They unite against Ruggedo, who diverts them through the forbidden Hollow Tube. On the far side of the world, Tititi-Hoochoo judges them innocent, appoints the dragon Quox to punish Ruggedo, and sends the group back through the Tube. Ruggedo resists their return, captures or transforms several companions, turns Shaggy Man into a dove, and threatens Tik-Tok. Polychrome awakens Quox, whose enchanted ribbon strips Ruggedo of his magic. Quox drives Ruggedo from the Nome Kingdom and makes Kaliko the new Nome King. The companions then seek the Ugly One in the Metal Forest. Queen Ann and her officers reappear there, Ruggedo is captured, and Shaggy finds his brother, whose ugliness resulted from Ruggedo’s enchantment. Polychrome’s fairy kiss restores him. Ruggedo repents and is allowed to remain as a harmless common nome. Ann abandons conquest and is returned to Oogaboo with her people and the Rose Princess. Ozma has the Wizard bring Betsy, Hank, Shaggy Man, his brother, and Tik-Tok to Oz. The story ends with Hank discovering he can speak in Oz, Ozma reconciling animals arguing over the sweetest girl, and Betsy happily wishing all children could live in Oz.

l: Queen Ann, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Queen Ann Soforth is the eldest daughter of Oogaboo's royal family and acts as Queen of Oogaboo while her mother searches for King Jol Jemkiph Soforth. Ambitious and dissatisfied with her tiny, poor kingdom, she rules from the royal palace, wears a green, gold-braided uniform and soldier-cap with a purple plume, and organizes and commands the Army of Oogaboo, including its officers, Private Soldier, and Tik-Tok. She plans to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz, and expects wealth, fame, plunder, and heroism; under the Army's arrangement, she is to receive half the plunder. She leads her army out of Oogaboo despite protests, resolves to conquer whatever territory they encounter, and claims land for Oogaboo. Her aggression falters when Hank defeats her attack and Private Files resigns, while the Love Magnet changes her anger into an embrace of Shaggy. She then joins a plan against Ruggedo. During the journey she faces the rubber terrain, crosses dry water, passes through the Tube, lands on a Peculiar Person, and regrets leaving Tititi-Hoochoo's rich country unconquered. Insisting that her Army, especially Tik-Tok, can conquer Ruggedo, she challenges General Guph, directs Tik-Tok's attack, and leads the party into underground caverns to conquer the Nome King and his people. The effort brings apparent imprisonment, escape, and hardship: she reaches the Metal Forest with her officers in torn clothes, a battered crown, and bruised limbs. Learning Ruggedo has been deposed, she asks about breaking the Ugly One's enchantment. Finally, she abandons conquest as too difficult, no longer wants to conquer the world, and earnestly wishes to return to Oogaboo. Ozma has the Wizard transport her and her people home.

l: Salye, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Salye, Ann Soforth's younger sister and Oogaboo royal family member, refuses palace sweeping, taunts Ann to conquer the Land of Oz, then swings in a hammock.

l: Queen Ann of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Queen Ann of Oogaboo, also called Ann Soforth, rules Oogaboo and commands its Army. Seeking to conquer the peaceful Land of Oz and replace Princess Ozma, she claims leadership of a party but is dismissed by the Private Citizen and frightened by Tititi-Hoochoo. She leads her Army into Ruggedo's Kingdom, falls into a pit with her officers, and discovers and uses an escape passage.

l: Ozma of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ozma is the gentle, beloved ruler of the Land of Oz, living in the Emerald City and placing her subjects first. Taller than Dorothy and Betsy, she governs without force: her tiny army is unarmed, and she once removed her sole soldier’s gun. Though initially unaware of Ann Soforth’s planned invasion while caring for her people, she can use the Magic Picture to observe distant events. Near the end, she uses the Wizard’s magic to return Queen Ann and the people of Oogaboo home, then admits Shaggy Man, his brother, Betsy, and Hank when Shaggy will not leave them. She welcomes the newcomers, values friendship over rivalry, reconciles Hank with the animals, and explains Oz’s spell on animal speech.

l: Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Oogaboo is a small, poor but pretty valley with orchards in a remote mountainous corner of the Land of Oz. Its eighty-nine people include eighteen men, twenty-seven women, and forty-four children, and it keeps a royal family as a matter of pride while remaining under Princess Ozma's rule. Queen Ann's Grand Army leaves through a narrow pass to conquer Ruggedo's Kingdom, but an altered route prevents its return. Regretting the loss of their orchards, Queen Ann and her people ultimately wish to go home, and Ozma sends them back to Oogaboo.

l: Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Land of Oz is a beautiful, lovely fairyland and Land of Love, ruled by Princess Ozma from the Emerald City and including Oogaboo. Though Ann judges its peaceful, unarmed officers and gentle people easy to overcome, the Army of Oogaboo’s campaign begins through a mountain pass and is stopped when Glinda redirects it elsewhere. By the end, Oz is a friendly place of gardens, fountains, and flowers where its fairy spell lets Hank and most animals speak.

l: world, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_targeted_for_conquest_by Ann Soforth Ann declares that she intends to conquer the world, beginning with the Land of Oz. She later imagines conquering other lands and possibly even the moon.

l: Army of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Army of Oogaboo is Queen Ann Soforth's force, assembled from seventeen recruits from Oogaboo for invasion and conquest. Jo Candy refuses to join; the remaining men are organized as four Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, four Captains, and the sole private, Jo Files. Though equipped with impressive uniforms, swords, and other weapons, its sixteen officers seek plunder with as little fighting as possible. Under Ann, it becomes lost in barren country, hungry and discouraged, encounters a Rak, and camps by a brook. It later approaches Shaggy and companions intending conquest, but Hank routs the officers. After seeing the Love Magnet, they become Shaggy's friends and agree to help conquer Ruggedo. Files resigns, and Tik-Tok replaces him as private; the army is thereafter described as mainly composed of Tik-Tok. Traveling with Ann toward the Nome Kingdom, it plans to seize metals and jewels and divide the spoils. It follows Tik-Tok through the Tube, emerges in disorder, restrains the Peculiar Person, and follows Tubekins after invisible beings kick it. Finally, marching in single column toward the nomes, Tik-Tok falls, and the officers enter Ruggedo's Kingdom, fall into a hidden pit, and are imprisoned with Ann.

l: Files, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Jo Files is a young, intelligent, ambitious man whose orchard produces steel files and story-books. He owns a gun, loaded with bullets from the Oogaboo bullet-tree, and intends to obtain a musket from a gun-tree. Though he prefers war and carnage, he is cheerful in hardship and keeps his engagement to help Ann Soforth conquer the world. He volunteers as the sole Private in Ann's Army, refusing officer rank and becoming a feared, trusted adviser to Queen Ann. During the march, he identifies a possible Rak, shoots it, and leads the Queen away when the officers flee. After planting Oogaboo's banner and declaring conquest, he refuses to bind harmless girls as slaves, resigning from the Army of Oogaboo rather than obey. He later guides adventurers, travels with Ozga and Polychrome, becomes friends with the Rose Princess, and is captured with her; Ruggedo handcuffs him to prevent an attack.

l: the Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Oogaboo expedition to conquer the world is Ann Soforth's purpose for Ann's Army. Ann begins by planning to surprise and intimidate Princess Ozma's peaceful, unarmed forces, replace Ozma as ruler, and avoid bloodshed. The army sets out to conquer unknown territory, then plans to take Ruggedo's kingdom, rescue Shaggy's brother, and seize its gold and jewels. After severe hardships, Queen Ann abandons the conquest, and Ozma sends the expedition back to Oogaboo.

l: Ann's venture, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a conquest attempt [against the Land of Oz and potentially other lands] Ann's venture begins when she leaves the palace to organize an army for her proposed conquest. She believes the venture cannot make her less happy than remaining in Oogaboo and accepts the risks in hopes of gaining greater power.

l: the officers of Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The officers of Oogaboo are sixteen immortal military officers, four Generals, four Colonels, four Majors, and four Captains, from the Army of Oogaboo. Traveling with Ann Soforth, they grow hungry, fretful, and disloyal, panic before the Rak, and run away. Marching behind Queen Ann, they fall into a concealed pit, escape through a secret passage, and later emerge from a rocky tunnel battered and in rags. In the Metal Forest, they capture Ruggedo, then release him after learning Kaliko is the new Nome King.

l: gun (Files's gun), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: contains bullets [gathered from an excellent bullet-tree in Oogaboo] Files's gun is loaded with large, hard bullets gathered from a bullet-tree in Oogaboo. He fires it at the Rak, breaking the creature's jaw, left wing, and right leg.

l: plunder, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Plunder drives Queen Ann Soforth's campaign: the army seeks it with minimal fighting, Ann links it to conquest and heroism, and half is assigned to her.

l: invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ann Soforth assembles the Army of Oogaboo for an invasion and conquest of the Land of Oz. Glinda prevents the army from reaching Oz by changing the route through the mountain pass.

l: mountain pass from Oogaboo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A mountain pass from Oogaboo originally leading to the Land of Oz and Fairyland of Oz is twisted by Glinda's magic, then disappears after the Army of Oogaboo emerges into adjoining territory.

l: army departure and march, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Army departure from Oogaboo begins as officers relay “For-ward March!”; Files leads, officers follow, and Queen Ann comes last through a narrow mountain pass toward Fairyland of Oz.

l: Glinda the Good, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Glinda the Good, Official Sorceress of the Kingdom of Oz, guards the Land of Oz's peace and happiness, owns and daily reads a Magic Record Book, then uses magic to block an army's planned entry by altering a mountain pass.

l: magic Record Book of the Sorceress Glinda, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a record book [magical; records every event anywhere as soon as it happens] Glinda's Magic Record Book records every event that takes place anywhere, from small incidents to great disasters. By reading it, Glinda learns that Ann Soforth has assembled an army to invade the Land of Oz.

l: adjoining territory, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The adjoining territory is a very beautiful country, distinct from the Land of Oz and separated by an invisible barrier. The Army of Oogaboo enters unknowingly, believing it has reached Oz; at dawn Betsy sees flowered banks and leafy trees, but no people.

l: Rak, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Rak is a terrible beast with a horrible appetite that flies, runs, and swims, breathes smoke from an internal furnace, and feeds on any living thing. Private Files shoots it, breaking its jaw, wing, and leg, but Rak cannot be killed by gunshot and says its injuries will heal.

l: the Army's journey, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The army's journey takes it through a barren, rocky country where it finds little food and becomes hopelessly lost. On the third day it encounters the Rak, then travels beyond the creature's smoky breath and camps by a brook.

l: the Rak's attack, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Rak's smoky breath darkens the sky and envelops the army, while its body falls upon the sixteen officers after Files shoots it. The Rak tries to crush and eat the army, but it rolls away from the officers, allowing them to escape.

l: magic, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Magic lets Glinda alter a mountain pass through a ceremony, diverting the Army of Oogaboo from the Land of Oz; it also powers the army's growing travel equipment. Later, Ruggedo loses his magic after seeing an enchanted ribbon, leaving him unable to use charms.

l: Betsy Bobbin, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Betsy Bobbin is a small, ordinary mortal girl from Oklahoma whose shipwreck begins her journey. Thrown into the sea when her ship strikes a rock, she saves herself by holding Hank's tail, reaches a floating hatch-cover with him, and rides the storm to land. Hungry and without a home, she and her faithful mule seek food and shelter, and Betsy consistently defends and cares for Hank. After meeting Shaggy Man, Betsy joins his search for his lost brother. She is brave, curious, independent, and kind: she refuses Queen Ann's claim that the party is conquered or must be enslaved; helps rescue and wind Tik-Tok; crosses dangers with Hank and her companions; asks questions of queens, dragons, and others without fear; and remains interested in what will happen even when others are frightened. She travels through the Rose Kingdom, the Rubber Country, the Hollow Tube, Queen Erma's land, and the Nome King's cavern, often riding Hank when tired. In the Nome King's cavern, Kaliko hides and kindly feeds Betsy, then restores her to her friends. She approves of Kaliko as king, judges Ruggedo harshly for his deeds but still urges leniency when he seems harmless, helps him gather jewels, brings him food and drink, and asks Kaliko not to be hard on him. She also bravely kisses the Ugly One to test whether the act will undo a charm. At the end, Betsy leaves the cavern with Hank, Shaggy Man, and Shaggy Man's brother. The Wizard brings her to the Land of Oz, where Dorothy welcomes her, Ozma gives her rooms, and the animals recognize her as Hank's beloved little mistress. Amazed by talking animals and delighted with Oz, she wishes every child could live there.

l: Hank, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Hank is Betsy Bobbin’s little, thin, sad-faced mule and donkey companion: shaggy, big-eared, long-tailed, harsh-voiced, short-tempered, but faithful, loyal, and protective. Thrown into the sea with Betsy, he swims to her raft, comforts her, promises to protect her, and remains awake while she sleeps. Ashore, his braying and temper bring conflict with the Royal Gardener and Roses; he eats an apple core, kicks the Gardener from the greenhouse, and leaves with Betsy, Shaggy Man, and Princess Ozga. He carries Betsy when she is tired, investigates a well, scatters Oogaboo’s officers with his heels, crosses the dry-water brook, and survives a rapid slide through the Hollow Tube with Betsy on his back. He later enters the Nome King’s cavern with Betsy and knocks down General Guph and the Nome King. After leaving the cavern, he reaches Oz, where he receives a cushioned stable stall. There he learns to speak animal speech, proudly defends Betsy, and is reconciled with the Sawhorse, Hungry Tiger, and Cowardly Lion.

l: ship, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A ship with a deck strikes a rock in a storm, throws Betsy and Hank overboard, catches fire, explodes, and sinks.

l: storm, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: wrecks ship The storm brings waves, lightning, and thunder while the ship is wrecked. It continues after the ship sinks, then wears itself out and passes away with distant growls.

l: sea, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Betsy and Hank fall into the dark blue sea after the ship strikes a rock. They float on the raft through the night, while the waves gradually become smaller and easier to ride.

l: raft (Betsy's and Hank's raft), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The raft is a hatch-cover torn from the ship's deck. After the ship is wrecked, Betsy pulls onto it and helps Hank aboard. Floating well enough to prevent their drowning, it carries them at sea and gently reaches the sandy beach with them.

l: shipwreck, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A storm causes the shipwreck when a ship strikes a rock, catches fire, explodes, and sinks; Betsy and Hank survive on floating wreckage and reach shore.

l: greenhouse, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A large, splendid greenhouse of crystal panes holds potted rosebushes with girls’ faces before a man falls through its roof.

l: Roses of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Roses of the Rose Kingdom are rare, fair, sweet-smelling but heartless beings, each with a lovely girl's face and thorns beneath green leaves. Awakened and frightened by Hank's bray, they demand that Betsy and Hank leave because only Roses belong there. Later they follow the Royal Gardener, oppose Princess Ozga as ruler, ignore the Love Magnet, and use thorns to drive the group out.

l: Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Rose Kingdom is a flower-strewn kingdom devoted to cultivating the rarest and fairest Roses, admitting only Roses and barring strangers. Once ruled by Ozga, it expelled her and others; after its last ruler withered early, the Royal Gardener governs temporarily. Its rulers grow on Royal Bushes, and its subjects seek a male Rose King. A deep gulf and drawbridge partly separate it.

l: Royal Gardener, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Royal Gardener is a wonderful, royal man and gardener who tends the Roses of the Rose Kingdom while temporarily ruling and enforcing its Law until a royal bush produces a ripe ruler. He wears a rose-colored costume, carries a spading fork and watering pot, and has small twinkling eyes. In the greenhouse, Hank’s bray frightens him into dropping the watering pot over Hank’s head and hiding behind the Roses. He condemns the strangers, becomes affectionate toward Shaggy Man through the Love Magnet, explains the missing Ruler, then allows the group to cross the drawbridge and returns to the greenhouse.

l: Law of the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Law of the Rose Kingdom governs its domains by forbidding strangers, including shipwrecked people, from entering. It requires the Ruler to condemn entering strangers to death and treats breaking greenhouse glass or intruding anywhere as violations. Though strangers enter, they leave before formal condemnation.

l: Shaggy Man, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Shaggy Man is a polite, mortal human man, an American who formerly lived in Colorado before going to the Land of Oz. He knows Ozma of Oz and Princess Dorothy, whom he calls an old chum. A traveler and companion of Betsy Bobbin, Hank, Ozga, Polychrome, Tik-Tok, Queen Ann, and others, he carries the Love Magnet, a magic talisman kept in his pocket, and believes it can win allies and even conquer Ruggedo. What matters most to him is rescuing his long-lost brother, the Ugly One, who has been unjustly imprisoned by Ruggedo. He has sought him for a long time, commands or urges an expedition against Ruggedo, offers the Army of Oogaboo plunder for its help, and repeatedly presses onward through dangers toward the Nome King's caverns. He also shows care for companions: he explains the Rubber Country and gravitation to Betsy, assists Tik-Tok and Tubekins, comforts others, and earnestly promises never to desert Betsy. His journey begins when he falls into the Rose Kingdom while seeking the hidden passage to Ruggedo's cavern. After leaving with Betsy, Hank, and Ozga, he gathers companions, discovers Tik-Tok, and learns more of his brother's captivity. He plans to use the Love Magnet against Ruggedo, but nomes bind him before he can draw it, and Ruggedo transforms him into a dove. Restored by touching Quox's ribbon, he continues demanding his brother's release and leads the search into the Metal Forest. There he finds the Ugly One, welcomes and comforts him without needing to see his face, and gives him a handkerchief and knife to make a mask. After the enchantment is broken, Shaggy rejoices in his brother's restored face and freedom. He remains faithful to Betsy and his brother, chooses their company rather than returning alone, mourns Polychrome's departure, and finally reaches the Land of Oz with Betsy, Hank, and his brother, crying tears of joy.

l: Rose Princess, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Rose Princess, named Ozga, is a Royal Princess of the Rose Kingdom and a Princess of Roseland, described as a ripe princess growing on a bush in the Royal Gardens. Picked by Betsy and Shaggy to rule, she is rejected by the Roses because they want a King and is exiled by her subjects. She joins Shaggy Man, Betsy, Hank, Polychrome, and Private Files in seeking Shaggy Man's lost brother and Ruggedo's kingdom, using the roadside flowers' guidance. Suspected of being a fairy and formerly a Fairy as a Mortal Maid, she later enters a cavern, is captured with Files, and tenderly cares for Shaggy Man after he becomes a dove.

l: Dorothy, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Dorothy is a girl and friend of Betsy Bobbin, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger. She owns Toto and possesses a silver whistle. She urges Ozma to welcome Betsy and Hank and save Shaggy Man’s group, warmly greets them, and delights when Toto finally speaks before running away.

l: the Ugly One, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Ugly One is Shaggy Man's lost brother, a miner who vanished in a Colorado gold mine about ten years earlier and was suspected by Shaggy Man of having been captured by the Nome King. He is held prisoner by Ruggedo in the Nome Kingdom, sent to the Metal Forest and unable to leave, though he is fed and rested. He does not work for the nomes because he can do nothing as well as they can. Once handsome, he is transformed by Ruggedo's enchantment into the homeliest man in the world. Ashamed and sensitive to ridicule, he hides in a hut and wears a polka-dot handkerchief as a mask. Shaggy Man and his companions seek the Metal Forest to free him. The Ugly One survives there on Three-Course Nuts and breakfast nuts. When Polychrome kisses him, the charm is broken: he is restored to his former appearance and recognized again as Shaggy Man's brother.

l: Nome King, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Nome King, also called the Metal Monarch and named Ruggedo, is king of the nomes who lives in an underground cavern, rules its caverns from a jeweled throne-room, and claims all metals hidden in the earth. Angry when people dig gold, he is suspected of capturing Shaggy Man's brother. When Queen Ann's group reaches his kingdom, he prepares a trap, orders Tik-Tok to hammer gold, and threatens Betsy Bobbin before Hank's kick leaves him flattened against a rock wall.

l: the Nome King's cavern, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: An underground cavern beneath earth in the Nome country, hidden from the Rainbow by concealed entrances. It contains the jeweled throne-room and Ruggedo's throne, where Tik-Tok challenges Ruggedo and later Betsy Bobbin, Hank, and General Guph arrive.

l: Royal Gardens, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: contains rosebushes [several enormous bushes] The Royal Gardens are enclosed by a tall hedge and contain enormous rosebushes on which the members of the Royal Family grow in various stages of maturity. The growing people appear green, lifeless, and unseeing until they are ripe and picked. Princess Ozga is found there fully ripe.

l: Love Magnet, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Love Magnet is a small silver horseshoe-shaped magic talisman whose charm makes those who see it love its owner, turning hatred into love. Shaggy Man uses it on the Royal Gardener, Hank, and the Army of Oogaboo, including Queen Ann, though the heartless Roses are unaffected. He hides it in his pocket; Ruggedo avoids seeing it, binds Shaggy’s arms, and transforms him into a dove.

l: Shaggy Man's search for his lost brother, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Shaggy Man searches for his lost brother after learning from Glinda’s magic Record Book that he disappeared. Believing him to be in the Nome King’s underground cavern, he travels with Betsy, Hank, and Princess Ozga. Their effort to free him brings the party against Ruggedo, who diverts them toward the Forbidden Tube. The brother is rescued from the Metal Forest, and Polychrome’s kiss removes his ugliness as the reunited group leaves for the outside world.

l: exile from the Rose Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: applies_to Princess Ozga [permanently] The Royal Gardener and the Roses force Shaggy Man, Betsy, Hank, and Princess Ozga out of the greenhouse and across the drawbridge. The group then enters the bleak, stony country beyond the Rose Kingdom and continues traveling together.

l: death sentence for strangers, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: applies_to strangers [entering the Rose Kingdom] The Royal Gardener announces that the Law requires every stranger entering the Rose Kingdom to be condemned to death. Because the kingdom has no current Ruler, no formal condemnation occurs, and the strangers ultimately escape by being expelled.

l: Polychrome, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Polychrome is the Rainbow's Daughter, a lovely, dainty sky fairy and daughter of the Rainbow, with her home in the skies and Cloud Palaces among her radiant sisters. Long-lived, beautiful, and reckless, she prefers dewdrops for food and is beyond Ruggedo's power to injure. After accidentally losing her Bow, she is stranded on earth when the Rainbow vanishes before she can return to it. Unable to find home, she joins the travelers opposing Ruggedo, despite not knowing the way to his cavern. She remains spirited and curious through danger: she dances when Hank routs the Army of Oogaboo, tests the Rubber Country by dancing, bounds over its stream, laughs during the Hollow Tube journey, and takes interest in the strange Kings and Queens gathered before Tititi-Hoochoo. As Queen Erma's guest, she rests, questions the inhabitants of the secluded fairyland, and receives dewdrops at the feast. Her most important role is aiding her earth friends against Ruggedo. She refuses his offer to stay, escapes his efforts to capture her, leaves to awaken Quox after Shaggy Man is transformed, and warns Quox that their friends are in danger. Watching daily for her father, she observes Ruggedo's hidden spring and leads the party through the passage he opened. Finally, out of gratitude for Shaggy Man's unselfish love for his brother, she kisses the Ugly One and breaks the charm of ugliness. Having finished helping her friends, she longs for the sky; when the Rainbow returns, she rides it home to her sisters, bidding her companions goodbye.

l: Rainbow, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Rainbow, carried by the Daughters of the Rainbow as their bow, appears over the barren country after rain. It carries Polychrome toward her sky home and Cloud Palaces, first leaving her stranded on earth, then later rescuing her from the Nome Kingdom and melting into clouds.

l: Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo is the Nome King, also called the Metal Monarch, an immortal ruler of the Nome Kingdom beneath the earth. A round little man with a white beard, red face, splendid robes, and a ruby crown, he owns the underground metals, gold, and jewels, rules from a jeweled cavern, and commands Kaliko and a Chief Magician. Proud of hatred and opposed to love, he is surly, cruel to the nomes, hostile to mortals and fairies, and possesses magic harmful to mankind. He keeps Shaggy Man’s brother prisoner, throws Tik-Tok into a well, forces travelers through the Forbidden Tube, and defies Tititi-Hoochoo’s warnings. When threatened by returning invaders, he refuses to free his prisoner, prepares the nome army, captures opponents, and uses transformations, including changing Shaggy Man into a dove. His power collapses when he looks at Quox’s enchanted ribbon: he loses his magic, fears eggs, and flees his cavern. Kaliko replaces him as king and takes his crown and sceptre. Reduced to a ragged, homeless wanderer, Ruggedo seeks jewels in the Metal Forest, but his overloaded pockets burst and he decides he no longer wants riches. He later returns humbly to the royal cavern, regrets his former wrongdoing, declares himself harmless, and promises good behavior so that he may remain underground. He is reformed, though no longer king or magical.

l: Tik-Tok, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Tik-Tok is a Smith & Tinker's Patent Double-Action, Extra-Responsive, Thought-Creating, Perfect-Talking Mechanical Man: a copper, clockwork man from the Land of Ev, moved by machinery and guaranteed to work for a thousand years. His thought, speech, and action mechanisms must be wound, and after water disables his joints he needs oil and drying. He cannot lie or think falsely because of his machinery, cannot fight, and can be injured only by a sledge hammer, though he carries a gun and a knapsack. Ozma sends him to guide and help Shaggy Man find his brother, but Ruggedo throws him into an old well. Shaggy Man and Betsy recover him and wind him up. He reluctantly becomes the Army of Oogaboo's only private soldier after Betsy promises to keep him wound, despite his inability to fight and concern that his works may run down. He is launched among rubber rocks, passes headfirst through the Hollow Tube, falls into a fountain, and is restored after Shaggy Man oils and dries him. His truthful account wins acceptance from the Private Citizen. On the way toward the nomes, he stubs his copper toe and needs help getting up. He reaches Ruggedo's throne-room, declares Ruggedo Queen Ann So-forth's prisoner, and raises his gun, but Kaliko knocks him down. Ruggedo and Guph weigh him down with a diamond and order him melted in a gold crucible. He later returns to Oz after faithfully serving Shaggy Man and the companions, praises Betsy, and supports admitting Shaggy Man's brother.

l: the Land of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A fairyland ruled by Ozma, it restricts mortal admission but ultimately admits Shaggy Man’s brother, Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Hank.

l: the earth's surface, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_destination_of Ruggedo [under the Jinjin's decree] The earth's surface is the place where the Jinjin commands Ruggedo to wander for all time. Ruggedo reaches it after fleeing his cavern but has no home, country, friend, follower, or wealth there.

l: the adventurers, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The adventurers are an honest group of mortals and immortals led by a shared effort to free Shaggy Man’s lost brother. Their party includes Betsy Bobbin, Hank, the Princess, Shaggy Man, and later Polychrome and Tik-Tok; it also travels at times with Queen Ann, the Army of Oogaboo, the Rose Princess, and Files. They become lost while seeking Ruggedo’s cavern, recover Tik-Tok, confront an approaching army, and continue toward the Nome Kingdom through the Rubber Country despite Ruggedo’s hindrance. Forced by Ruggedo through the Forbidden Tube, they are judged innocent, hosted by Kings and Queens, and finally ordered to return through the Tube to their own side of the world.

l: the Nome Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Nome Kingdom is an underground world beneath the mountains, home to countless nomes and rich in metals and precious stones. It contains the Nome King's royal cavern, Ruggedo's jeweled cavern, the Great Domed Cavern, and the Metal Forest. At first Ruggedo rules it with absolute sway, guarding it against Shaggy, the Army of Oogaboo, Queen Ann's forces, and other approaching adventurers; its gloomy entrance passage has traps and secret ways, and the invaders are captured or scattered. Ruggedo offers Polychrome a place there, but she refuses. The Jinjin's decree drives Ruggedo out, and eggs prevent his return. Quox appoints Kaliko King, whom the nomes prefer. Later Ruggedo may remain only under Kaliko's supervision as the companions return.

l: Kaliko, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Kaliko is a highly intelligent nome who begins as Ruggedo's loyal Royal Chamberlain and High Chamberlain, serving as an official and carrying out orders even when he foresees that Ruggedo's choices will ruin him. He uses the Magic Spyglass to watch the approaching adventurers, warns Ruggedo about Tititi-Hoochoo and the forbidden Hollow Tube, and advises releasing the Shaggy Man's brother. Though he sometimes acts covertly, kicking Tik-Tok's knee-joints, he also protects and assists others: he shelters Betsy Bobbin and Hank in his furnished room, feeds Betsy, and organizes nomes for Ruggedo's plans. He repeatedly offers prudent counsel, including that Tik-Tok is valuable, but Ruggedo disregards or threatens him. After the rescue, Kaliko becomes the new King of the Nome Kingdom, ruling Nome Country and responsible for its subjects. He leads the group back through the Metal Forest, provides refreshments, and permits the formerly served Ruggedo to remain only if he behaves, with exile promised for further misconduct.

l: the nomes, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The nomes are numerous subterranean people throughout the Nome Kingdom, laboring endlessly in caverns to hammer metals, melt ores, polish gems, and build the Metal Forest. They possess magic spears and serve under Ruggedo, General Guph, and later King Kaliko. They hate and fear Ruggedo, yet obey his commands: capturing travelers, imprisoning Queen Ann and her officers, binding and guarding prisoners, serving as executioners, searching for escapees, and pulling a chain to restrain Quox. Their greatest terror is eggs; contact with an egg's inside can destroy a nome unless a magical word is spoken quickly. Eggs drive them, along with Guph, Kaliko, Pang, and executioners, back into the caverns. After Ruggedo's rule, the chief nomes swear obedience to Kaliko, and the nomes are expected to welcome the change, help seek passages to the Metal Forest, and expel Ruggedo after he takes his permitted treasure. They are also mischievous, discouraging nearby settlement.

l: Tititi-Hoochoo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Tititi-Hoochoo, also called the Great Jinjin and the Private Citizen, is a fairy and Jinjin who is the supreme ruler of a land on the other side of the world. Revered by Kings and Queens, he occupies the throne and rules with authority, superior powers, high Reason, and Justice. He has black eyes with red sparks, no heart, and a white robe bearing a dragon’s head; he is terrible to wrong-doers but never judges without reason. After warning Ruggedo against using the Hollow Tube again, he learns that Ruggedo forced travelers through the Forbidden Tube. He treats the travelers as innocent guests, declares Ruggedo responsible, and orders their return through the Tube. He selects Quox to punish Ruggedo, then uses an enchanted ribbon to strip Ruggedo of magic and decrees Ruggedo’s exile from the Nome Kingdom to wander the earth’s surface.

l: Long-Eared Hearer, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Long-Eared Hearer is a nome and Hearer with enormous, unusually long ears that can detect distant voices with exceptional precision. Serving Ruggedo, he reports adventurers, Shaggy Man, and Oogaboo's army, suffers Ruggedo's cruel ear-twisting, escapes, then later tracks returning invaders through the Hollow Tube. He cannot hear eggs, and Ruggedo's sceptre breaks the tip of one ear.

l: the Rubber Country, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Rubber Country is a landscape of gray rubber rocks, trees, paths, stepping-stones, and dry-water stream; touching it makes adventurers bounce as they wade across.

l: the Forbidden Tube, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Forbidden Tube, also called the Hollow Tube, is a steep, smooth metal passage with a hole through the earth, passing through its center and leading to the other side of the world. Built by Hiergargo the Magician for exclusive use, it is private property, forbidden to intruders, and marked at its mouth with warnings that outsiders stay out and those inside not come out. Entering or using it brings a punishment of nine days and ten nights of torture before being thrown back into it. Ruggedo has the Chief Magician redirect a path to its concealed opening and plans to drop the adventurers through it. It sends them at great speed for more than an hour and ejects them into a garden. Later it carries them back from Tititi-Hoochoo's land; Tititi-Hoochoo forbids rubbish from being thrown into it, and Quox finally shoots into open air above its entrance.

l: Metal Forest, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Metal Forest is an artificial forest in the Great Domed Cavern, the largest cavern in the Nome Kingdom, within a vast dome beneath another mountain. Created by Ruggedo to keep precious metals from mortals, it has trees of gold and silver, solid-gold trunks, branches, and leaves, filigree-silver bushes and underbrush, jewel-strewn ground, and paths sometimes paved with diamonds. It also contains a green grove of natural trees and, beyond its metal growth, ordinary food-bearing trees. Ruggedo sends and holds the Ugly One there, protected by secret entrances that change weekly, though even Ruggedo cannot always find it. Later Queen Ann and the officers of Oogaboo enter through a tunnel and are trapped. After the Ugly One is rescued, the group crosses the forest; the officers collect jewels, and a jewel trail leads outward through the passage after Ruggedo drops them.

l: the adventurers' journey to the Nome Kingdom, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The adventurers follow a winding route toward the mountains where the entrance to Ruggedo's cavern is located. They cross the Rubber Country and continue toward the Nome Kingdom despite Ruggedo's attempts to stop them.

l: the crossing of the Rubber Country, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: During the crossing, Tik-Tok and two officers are bounced by the rubber stepping-stones. Polychrome and Betsy Bobbin bound over the brook, Hank falls into the dry water, and the entire party eventually wades across and continues onward.

l: the magic spyglass, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The magic spyglass lets Kaliko see through the Hollow Tube’s curves; in Chapter Fourteen, he twists it with a charm to watch invaders falling through the Tube.

l: Ruggedo's rage, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo's rage begins when he senses mortals approaching his kingdom. He raves, kicks Kaliko, attacks the Long-Eared Hearer, chases Kaliko around the throne, and finally insists on using the Hollow Tube against the invaders.

l: the Army of Oogaboo's planned treasure raid, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Army of Oogaboo plans to capture the Nome Kingdom's gold, metals, and jewels, then divide and carry the spoils among officers and Queen Ann.

l: the attempted attack with the Hollow Tube, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_opposed_by Tititi-Hoochoo [because Ruggedo defies his warning] Ruggedo orders the adventurers' path to be turned toward the Hollow Tube so they will fall through its invisible opening. The plan is carried out by Kaliko and the Chief Magician, even though Kaliko warns that it defies Tititi-Hoochoo.

l: Tubekins, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Tubekins is a beautiful but expressionless King of the Tube, with large blue eyes, bushy black hair, multicolored skin, and a scarlet dragon-embroidered robe. He directs invisible inhabitants and treats the Tube as private property. While hoeing pink violets, he is struck by Queen Ann’s landing and crown, then questions the travelers. Later he escorts the adventurers to the Forbidden Tube, orders them inside, waits for Quox, and remains behind as their journey begins.

l: invisible inhabitants, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Invisible inhabitants, an unseen but audible group, surround arrivals, move objects, aid Tik-Tok with an oil-can, then propel Ann and hesitant officers to follow Tubekins.

l: journey through the Tube, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The journey through the Tube lasts more than an hour, moving darkly and extremely fast through the earth. It begins as fearful and frightening, then becomes longer but more comfortable, letting travelers talk before they emerge into daylight at the mountain above the Nome King's caverns.

l: the party's arrival through the Forbidden Tube, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The party unknowingly falls into the Forbidden Tube in separate groups and slides through it. Ruggedo causes their arrival in the land, which the Private Citizen judges forced rather than a willing violation of its laws.

l: the country of the Private Citizen, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A beautiful garden on the other side of the world, opposite where travelers entered the Tube; they arrive, encounter Tubekins and unfamiliar customs, then follow Tubekins toward an immense castle.

l: Queen Erma, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Queen Erma, Queen of Light, rules her fairyland and loves six messengers; she welcomes Betsy and Polychrome, explains her land, hosts a feast, and has Electra show Betsy to a chamber.

l: Kings and Queens, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Kings and Queens are hundreds in the Private Citizen's country, resembling Tubekins and wearing scarlet robes and jeweled crowns. Equal yet subject to him, they bow, receive travelers as guests, and escort them to palaces.

l: the Residence, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Residence belongs to the Private Citizen, contains the village of palaces, and is where he questions the party and orders travelers returned after entertainment.

l: the condemnation of Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_pending decision by Private Citizen The Private Citizen determines that Ruggedo is to blame for forcing the party through the Forbidden Tube and says that he alone must be punished. He has not yet decided the form of punishment and plans to determine it before the party returns the next day.

l: Sunlight, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Sunlight, first among the six messengers of light, is radiantly beautiful, wears silvery-white robes, and gives strength and energy to mortals and fairies.

l: Moonlight, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Moonlight, second of the six messengers of light, is a soft, dreamy damsel in silvery-white robes who replaces Daylight and cheers mortals and fairies.

l: Starlight, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Starlight, third of the six messengers of light, is a lovely, retiring, shy maiden in shimmering silvery-white robes who replaces Moonlight beside Erma when the moon is hidden.

l: Daylight, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Daylight, fourth of six messengers of light, is a brilliant, frank, laughing-eyed damsel in many colors; beside Erma, she yields to Moonlight and cannot replace Sunlight.

l: Firelight, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A fifth messenger of light, Firelight appears in a fleecy flame-colored robe beside Erma after Starlight, bringing warmth, comfort, and cheer inside houses.

l: Electra, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Electra, sixth and most beautiful of the six messengers of light, is envied by Sunlight and Daylight; as old as the other lights, she floods mortals and fairies with rays when they fail, then shows Betsy her chamber.

l: the Original Dragon, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Original Dragon is the first living creature ever made, the oldest and wisest of living things, and the fairyland's original resident. Since the world's creation it remembers everything, remaining in the fairyland and supplying wisdom whenever its inhabitants need it.

l: the six messengers of light, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Six lovely maidens, Sunlight, Moonlight, Starlight, Daylight, Firelight, and Electra, serve Erma, greet Betsy and Polychrome, attend a feast, and benefit mortals and fairies.

l: fairies, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Fairies minister to mankind, live in Erma's fairyland, and revere Tititi-Hoochoo, wearing dragon-head emblems of connection to favored inhabitants.

l: the fairyland ruled by Erma, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The fairyland is a beautiful, secluded country inhabited by fairies and ruled by Tititi-Hoochoo, while Erma is its Queen of Light. It is said to nearly equal the Fairyland of Oz in beauty and surpass it in power.

l: Quox, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Quox is a huge, young, enormous blue dragon of the highly respected Dragon Family, three thousand and fifty-six years old at the time of his return journey. He has silver scales, fire inside him, brimstone breath, claws and teeth, flame-breathing power, and an electric light at the end of his tail. Strong, fierce, good-natured, conceited, and fond of his own voice, he wears forty yards of enchanted ribbon and a great jeweled locket around his neck. After disrespecting the Original Dragon, he is made Tititi-Hoochoo’s messenger and Instrument of Vengeance. He serves Jinjin and is ordered to conquer Ruggedo. Carrying the travelers and invaders as a beast of burden through the Tube, he protects them from nomes’ spears with his tough silver-scaled body, then waits outside the caverns and cannot be awakened from his trance. In Ruggedo’s cavern, a thousand nomes chain him, but the enchanted ribbon removes Ruggedo’s magic. Quox announces Jinjin’s decree, uses eggs from his locket to drive Ruggedo away, breaks enchantments on the Rose Princess and Shaggy Man, breaks his own chains, and appoints Kaliko King of the Nomes, expecting wise rule. With his mission finished, he returns headfirst through the Tube toward his home on the other side of the world, planning to sleep until he arrives.

l: the Shaggy Man's brother, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Shaggy Man's brother, a kindly, honest fellow, is held prisoner by Ruggedo after years imprisoned by the Nome King, then recovered and freed from ugliness; Ozma admits him to Oz with Shaggy Man and others.

l: underground caverns of the Nome King, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The underground caverns beneath the mountain shelter the nomes and their treasure. After the nomes retreat there, Queen Ann plans an entry; later, Kaliko gives visitors rooms, and a hidden passage behind a rock leads to the Metal Forest's treasure.

l: the Instrument of Vengeance, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is Quox [the royal instrument selected by Tititi-Hoochoo] The Instrument of Vengeance is to accompany the adventurers through the Forbidden Tube and punish Ruggedo on Tititi-Hoochoo's behalf. Quox is selected for this role because of his disrespect toward the Original Dragon.

l: Ruggedo's punishment, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo is punished for defying Tititi-Hoochoo and misusing the Forbidden Tube: he is driven from his underground caverns, stripped of magic powers, and made a homeless wanderer.

l: the Jinjin's judgment, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Jinjin’s judgment clears the adventurers, blames Ruggedo alone, condemns him to leave the Nome Kingdom and wander permanently without home, country, companions, followers, or wealth beyond his pockets, and assigns Quox an unpleasant mission as punishment for disrespect.

l: the adventurers' return journey, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The adventurers’ return journey begins riding Quox through the Forbidden Tube, from Tititi-Hoochoo to the other side of the world, as Quox slows from extreme speed to a comfortable slide through darkness.

l: the invaders, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: seek the invaders' conquest of the Metal Monarch [including seizure of his treasure and expulsion from his dominions] The invaders are returning through the Hollow Tube after being thrown down it by Ruggedo. They intend to conquer the Metal Monarch, seize his treasure, and drive him from his dominions. Kaliko sees them riding on the back of a dragon.

l: General Guph, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: General Guph is the Nome King’s famous general and leader of Ruggedo’s forces. Ordered to summon, arm, and lead the nome army to the Hollow Tube, he commands an attack on the travelers, angrily orders them captured, and has spears thrown. He warns Tik-Tok, tries to seize Betsy, but Hank kicks him into the Nome King. Later he fetches the Long-Eared Hearer and unsuccessfully helps pursue Polychrome.

l: the Nome King's conquest, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The conquest is Queen Ann and the Army of Oogaboo's attempted invasion of the Nome King to defeat the Metal Monarch, seize his treasure, and drive him from his dominions. Ruggedo summons the nome army; Queen Ann and officers are trapped and Tik-Tok is knocked down, so it fails, though several invaders escape and weaken Ruggedo's control.

l: the eggs, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Eggs are the objects most feared by the nomes because their insides are fatal when they touch them. Possibly enchanted by Tititi-Hoochoo, they do not come through the Hollow Tube at first, then roll from a jeweled locket, pursue Ruggedo, drive him out, and bar the Nome Kingdom.

l: the nome army's planned attack, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: targets the invaders [at the mouth of the Tube] Ruggedo orders General Guph to summon and arm the nome army. The nomes are to march to the mouth of the Hollow Tube and seize the invaders as soon as they appear.

l: mountain-side (Nome Kingdom), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: contains the caverns of the nomes Polychrome sits on the mountain each day to watch for the Rainbow. Ruggedo repeatedly approaches the mountain's cavern entrance before discovering the concealed passage.

l: the nomes' attack, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: uses magic spears The nomes' attack consists of hundreds of sharp magic spears thrown at the travelers. Quox moves in front of the group and his silver scales stop the spears, which then return to the nomes' hands.

l: the big pit, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The big pit is a covered trap and prison inside the rocky passage to the jeweled throne-room. It is opened to capture Queen Ann and her officers, then covered by the nomes; later, its supposed prisoners have vanished although the cover remains.

l: the Slimy Cave, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a cave [a named underground location] The Slimy Cave is searched for Betsy Bobbin and Hank, but Pang reports that no one is inside.

l: the capture of Queen Ann and the officers, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a imprisonment [in the pit] Queen Ann and the officers are captured after they fall into the open pit in the passage to Ruggedo's throne-room. They remain trapped until Queen Ann finds a secret opening leading to an underground passage.

l: the escape passage, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: An underground passage begins behind a secret opening in the pit, dark, damp, narrow, twisting, and too low to stand in, as Queen Ann and officers crawl toward freedom.

l: royal cavern (Nome King's cavern), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo's jeweled underground royal cavern in the Nome Kingdom contains his throne and serves as the setting for prisoners, executions, royal entertainment, confrontations, and magic against captives. He flees it from pursuing eggs, then later returns cautiously as the party reunites and receives Kaliko's refreshments.

l: gold crucible, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_used_to_melt Tik-Tok [when heated white-hot] Ruggedo orders the gold crucible to be heated to a white, seething heat so that Tik-Tok can be dumped into it and melted.

l: dove (Shaggy Man), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a dove [the transformed Shaggy Man] The dove is Shaggy Man after Ruggedo's sorcery transforms him. Once freed from its tiny cords, it flies upward and settles on the Rose Princess's shoulder.

l: Shaggy Man's transformation, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo performs unlawful sorcery, waving seven semicircles and speaking magic wugwa to instantly transform Shaggy Man into a dove.

l: hatred and love, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: are opposites [Ruggedo is proud of one and abhors the other] Ruggedo is proud of his hatred and abhors love. He fears that seeing the Love Magnet would turn his hatred into love, but he claims to like Polychrome and offers her a place in his kingdom.

l: Polychrome's friends, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: are_captured_by Ruggedo [in the jeweled cavern] Polychrome says that Ruggedo has captured her friends and is about to destroy them. Ruggedo has transformed the Rose Princess into a fiddle and is about to transform Files into a fiddle bow when Quox interrupts him.

l: the great jeweled locket, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Attached to the pearl necklace around Quox’s neck, the great jeweled locket opens to release six eggs that drive Ruggedo from the Nome Kingdom.

l: the enchanted ribbon, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: removes magic [from anyone who looks upon it] The enchanted ribbon is worn around Quox's neck and was prepared by Tititi-Hoochoo. When Ruggedo looks at it, he loses his magical powers and cannot perform even familiar spells.

l: Ruggedo's exile, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo's exile begins when eggs drive him from his cavern; deprived of kingdom and wealth, Kaliko orders him from the nomes' country forever, leaving him a wandering outcast.

l: King Kaliko, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: King Kaliko is a Metal Monarch and former Royal Chamberlain who becomes the new Nome King after Ruggedo flees and falls. Kind to Betsy Bobbin during her captivity and friendly to the officers of Oogaboo, he is praised by Betsy, made King by Quox, and takes Ruggedo’s throne, ruby crown, and sceptre. He appoints Guph as Royal Chamberlain, rules the Nome Kingdom and its cavern, and directs the nomes to seek a passage to the Metal Forest and pursue Ruggedo. Although he plans to expel Ruggedo after permitting him treasure, Kaliko assures Queen Ann of friendship, grants freedom to the Ugly One, and cannot undo the enchantment of his appearance.

l: the secret passages to the Metal Forest, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The secret passages to the Metal Forest are three weekly changing routes controlled by Ruggedo, linking the nomes’ caverns, the Metal Forest, and the outer world. After a three-day failed search, Polychrome sees Ruggedo open one and leads the others through; it later lies dark, jewel-strewn, then opens to daylight when the charm breaks.

l: the enchantment of ugliness, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_broken_by the kiss of a Fairy [specifically by Polychrome's kiss] The charm of ugliness was cast by Ruggedo on Shaggy Man's brother, transforming him from a handsome man into the Ugly One. It is finally broken by the kiss of a Fairy.

l: Kaliko's accession as King, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Kaliko is approved by Tititi-Hoochoo, welcomed by delighted nomes, made Metal Monarch and King by Quox, takes the throne, and appoints Guph Royal Chamberlain.

l: Ruggedo's flight and exile, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Ruggedo escapes from the royal cavern after the eggs and enchantments are removed. The characters regard him as gone for good, and Kaliko succeeds him as King of the Nomes.

l: the rescue of the Ugly One, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_planned_by Shaggy Man [after learning his brother's location] The rescue of the Ugly One has not yet occurred. Shaggy Man and the others intend to search for one of Ruggedo's secret passages to the Metal Forest so they can free him.

l: the Metal Forest's treasure, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a vast treasure hoard [greater than the treasure in the rest of the world except possibly Oz] The Forest contains more treasure than the rest of the world, except perhaps the land of Oz. Its riches include gold trees, silver vegetation, scattered precious gems, and diamond-paved paths.

l: Quox's departure, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a return journey [to Quox's home] Quox bids farewell to the group and returns through the Tube to his own country. The others thank him for befriending them and feel that they have lost a kind and sociable friend.

l: the search for the hidden passages, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: lasts three days [before Ruggedo's passage is found] After Quox leaves, the group resumes searching for passages to the Metal Forest, but the effort fails for three days. The search succeeds only after Polychrome notices and copies Ruggedo's method of opening one.

l: Ruggedo's discovery of the passage, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: reveals the hidden passages to the Metal Forest [through a rock-operated entrance] Ruggedo recalls the Metal Forest and realizes that he alone knows how to reach it. He touches a spring in a rock, opens a broad passage, enters it, and swings the rock shut behind him, unaware that Polychrome is watching.

l: secret tunnel (Metal Forest), Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A secret passage to Metal Forest, hardest of three, begins as a jagged rock-lined route and ends with Queen Ann and officers escaping bruised and with torn clothing.

l: Ugly One's hut, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_made_of twigs and golden branches [woven together] The Ugly One's hut is a small shelter made of twigs and golden branches in the grove of natural trees. He hides inside it and initially refuses to come out, but later opens the door after making a mask.

l: Ruggedo's enchantment, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: makes Ugly One (Shaggy Man's brother) [physically repulsive] Ruggedo's enchantment changes the Ugly One from a handsome man into an extremely ugly one. Kaliko does not know how to break it, and the Ugly One believes he must remain masked because of it.

l: freedom from the nomes, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_granted_by Kaliko [to Ugly One (Shaggy Man's brother)] Kaliko grants the Ugly One freedom from the nomes after becoming the new Nome King. The Ugly One still fears accepting that freedom because he is ashamed of his altered appearance.

l: Ugly One's mask, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_made_of red handkerchief [covered with big white polka dots and cut for the eyes and nostrils] The Ugly One's mask is made from Shaggy Man's red handkerchief with large white polka dots. It has holes for his eyes and nostrils and allows him to face the others without showing his features.

l: the officers' capture of Ruggedo, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The officers of Oogaboo capture Ruggedo after discovering him in the Metal Forest. They believe he is still the Nome King, but release him when Files explains that Kaliko has replaced him.

l: the kiss of a Mortal Maid, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: does_not_break the charm of ugliness [Betsy's kiss fails] Ruggedo recalls that the kiss of a Mortal Maid might break the charm of ugliness. Betsy, a Mortal Maid, kisses the Ugly One, but Ruggedo determines that her kiss does not break the charm.

l: the kiss of a Fairy, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: breaks the charm of ugliness [required antidote] Ruggedo suggests that the kiss of a Fairy may be required to break the charm of ugliness. Polychrome gives this kiss, and it restores Shaggy Man's brother.

l: Ruggedo's reform, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_a reformation [of Ruggedo] Ruggedo's reform is shown by his admission that he is sorry, his claim that he is harmless, and his promise to behave as a common nome. The others are pleased to hear that he has really reformed, though Betsy hopes he will keep his word.

l: the Wizard of Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A wizard of Oz possessing magic, he invents a wireless telephone, watches adventurers with Ozma, and transports Oogaboo's people, the Rose Princess, Shaggy Man, companions to homes and Oz.

l: the Magic Picture, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Magic Picture, framed by radium in Ozma's boudoir, shows scenes Ozma chooses with moving figures; Ozma and the Wizard watch adventurers until it shows their transport to Oz.

l: the Wizard's magic, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: can_transport people [across great distances] The Wizard's magic can transport people over great distances and enables Ozma to send Queen Ann's party home. He uses pink powder, an incantation, a silver plate, and perfumed smoke to bring Shaggy Man's group to Oz.

l: the magic transport, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The magic transport carries Betsy Bobbin and Shaggy Man’s brother to Oz, then returns the people of Oogaboo and the Rose Princess home before bringing Shaggy Man, his brother, Betsy Bobbin, and Hank to Oz.

l: the Land of Oz's admission policy, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: restricts mortals [because Oz is fairyland] The Land of Oz's admission policy treats admitting mortals as a serious matter and does not make Oz a refuge for every mortal in distress. Ozma makes an exception for Shaggy Man's brother so that Shaggy Man, Betsy, and Hank can also be welcomed.

l: the Sawhorse, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Sawhorse, an alive wooden horse and Ozma's favorite steed, is the only horse in the Land of Oz, shod with gold plates and housed in Ozma's palace. He speaks animal speech, praises Ozma, then accepts Hank as a friend.

l: the Cowardly Lion, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: A cowardly lion, Dorothy’s first friend and companion, rests in Ozma’s stable, calls Dorothy the sweetest girl, then accepts Hank as a friend and offers help or advice.

l: the Hungry Tiger, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: The Hungry Tiger, a tiger living in Emerald City, loves Dorothy and joins the Cowardly Lion defending her; after watching Hank, he rubs noses with him and becomes reconciled.

l: Toto, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: Toto is a little shaggy black dog from Kansas who understands speech, usually communicates with barks and his tail, and finally proves he can speak when Dorothy asks.

l: Land of Love, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: values friendship [above every other quality] The Land of Oz is described as a Land of Love in which friendship outranks every other quality. Its inhabitants must be friends in order to retain the love of the land.

l: friendship, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: outranks love [in the Land of Oz] Friendship is declared more important than competing claims about which girl is sweetest. Ozma uses this principle to reconcile Hank, the Sawhorse, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger.

l: love, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_required_by Land of Oz [for retaining the land's love] Love is shown through the loyalty of Hank to Betsy, the animals' devotion to Dorothy or Ozma, and the welcome extended to friends in Oz. Ozma says that the Land of Oz is a Land of Love and that its inhabitants must be friends to retain its love.

l: animal speech in Oz, Tik-Tok of Oz
s: is_available_to the animals of Oz [almost universally] Animals in Oz generally speak, and Hank begins speaking as soon as he enters the land. Toto is an exception by choice: although the spell lets him speak words and he understands everything said to him, he prefers barks, tail signals, and silence.

l: The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The document is an adventure story following Trot and Cap’n Bill, longtime companions whose coastal cave exploration becomes an extraordinary journey through strange lands and into Oz. Their small boat is caught by a Great Whirlpool, which sweeps them into an underwater cavern. There they meet Flipper, an Ork from Orkland, who carries them through an underground gulf and tunnel to an island. After dealing with the island’s unhappy ruler Pessim and using size-changing lavender and purple berries, Trot and Cap’n Bill travel in the Ork’s sunbonnet across the ocean to the Land of Mo. They meet the Bumpy Man, find Button-Bright buried in warm popcorn snow, enlarge birds with berries, and fly across a desert into Jinxland. In Jinxland, they learn that King Krewl cruelly rules despite Princess Gloria’s rightful claim. Gloria loves Pon, a gardener’s boy who is actually the son of King Phearse, while Krewl seeks to force her to marry Googly-Goo. Krewl and the witch Blinkie imprison Gloria, turn Cap’n Bill into a gray grasshopper with a wooden leg, and freeze Gloria’s heart so she cannot love Pon. Trot, Pon, Button-Bright, and Cap’n Bill receive help when Glinda sends the Scarecrow from Oz. After Button-Bright is found by the returning Ork, the Scarecrow confronts Krewl. Krewl tries to have him burned, but Orks rescue him, defeat Krewl’s forces, and place the Scarecrow on the throne. The Scarecrow compels Blinkie to restore Cap’n Bill and Gloria’s heart, then removes her magic. Gloria becomes Queen, names Pon her Royal Consort, and Krewl is spared but made a gardener’s boy called Grewl. The travelers leave Jinxland with the Scarecrow and Orks, entering Oz. Ozma, Dorothy, and Betsy Bobbin have already watched their danger through the Magic Picture and arrange welcome and shelter. On the way to Glinda’s palace, the Scarecrow falls into a waterfall and is rescued from the Ruby Cavern, though he must be restuffed with fresh straw. Finally, Glinda welcomes the party, Ozma receives Trot and Cap’n Bill at the Emerald City with a banquet and reception, and Button-Bright wanders away again, though Ozma says he cannot go far astray in Oz.

l: Cap'n Bill, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Cap'n Bill is an old, one-legged sailor-man with a grizzled fringe of hair, a mostly bald head, pale blue gentle eyes, and a rugged bronzed face. After losing his left leg below the knee, he stops sailing and lives as a star boarder with Trot's mother, using saved money for his keep. He has loved Trot since she was a baby, teaches her almost everything she knows, and is her faithful companion. Strong and skilled at rowing, practical with food, gear, candles, and shelter, he is also cautious but brave and protective. When a Great Whirlpool takes Trot and him from their boat into an undersea cavern, he tries to shield her, then helps her survive by fishing, cooking, and leading their exploration with the Ork. Though afraid of the unknown tunnel and conscious of diminishing supplies, he travels onward, reaches the surface, investigates new lands, and accepts magical shrinking so the Ork can carry him and Trot over the ocean. He returns to normal size, preserves remaining magic berries, and continues through mountains and Jinxland with Trot, Button-Bright, and the Ork. In Jinxland, he questions what he sees, aids Pon, boldly requests food and rooms from King Krewl, and is transformed while asleep by Blinkie into a grasshopper with a wooden leg. He escapes, remains useful in grasshopper form, and is eventually restored; his match helps enable the spell that melts Gloria's frozen heart. He thanks the Ork, travels safely to the Land of Oz, and is admired for not grumbling over his transformation. There he continues helping his companions, notably rescuing and restoring the Scarecrow after his fall into water. Comfortable and free from danger, Cap'n Bill hopes to live in Oz with Trot, with a cosy room next to hers overlooking the gardens.

l: Trot, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Trot is a very little girl from California, a child with big, solemn eyes and an earnest, simple manner. Cap'n Bill has taught her almost everything she knows; he is her close friend, companion, and trusted guardian. Though small, she is brave, practical, and compassionate. She steers their boat as a Great Whirlpool draws them in, survives the underwater journey with Cap'n Bill, and insists they explore their cavern refuge rather than wait to starve. With Cap'n Bill and the Ork, she travels through tunnels, over an island, and through the Land of Mo, enduring hunger, weariness, shrinking and regaining her size, and flights on the Ork and giant birds. In Jinxland, Trot travels with Cap'n Bill, Button-Bright, and later Pon. She sympathizes deeply with Princess Gloria and Pon after learning of King Krewl's cruelty, distrusts the King and Lord Googly-Goo, comforts Gloria after freeing her from her room, and continues searching when Cap'n Bill and Button-Bright disappear. She helps the Scarecrow after Blinkie destroys his body, recognizes Cap'n Bill in the form of a grasshopper, supports action against Blinkie, and joyfully embraces Cap'n Bill when he is restored. She also helps care for the Scarecrow during the journey onward. Trot ultimately reaches the Land of Oz with her companions. She is safe there, becomes friends with Dorothy and Betsy Bobbin, receives a room next to Dorothy at Ozma's Royal Palace, and hopes to live in Oz always with Cap'n Bill because she cannot at present return to the outside world.

l: whirlpool, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: A whirlpool in the sea begins when a whirl in the air creates a powerful swirl in the water. It slopes the ocean into a great basin with a black central hole, drawing a boat around its edge and inward. It captures the Ork and carries Trot and Cap'n Bill into a cavern.

l: the ocean, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The ocean is a blue, glassy, great body of salt water and a large body of water. It becomes dangerously still in the hot afternoon and, near the Great Whirlpool, forms a rapidly rotating basin around a dark hole. It carries Trot and Cap'n Bill through the hole and still, cool depths connected to a cavern pool. Later it is seen as blue waves beyond the forest and below the Ork's flight, surrounding an island while the Ork searches its horizon for land.

l: the boat, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: is_moored_to the cable [at the water's edge] The boat belongs to Cap'n Bill and is moored to a rock by a stout cable before Cap'n Bill and Trot take it toward the caves. The Great Whirlpool catches the boat, carries it around the circular basin, and pulls it progressively closer to the central hole despite Cap'n Bill's efforts to escape.

l: the cavern under the sea, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The cavern under the sea is a warm, lonely, dome-like prison and the Ork’s former cavern. It holds rugged rocks, a sandy beach rising from a pool, seaweed, and a bluish-green glow, but no outside entrance; its only outlet is water. Trot and Cap’n Bill fall into it, dry their clothes, cook fish, and sleep, then are trapped there. The Ork arrives through submerged caverns, and a sloping passage leads to a black hole and precipice above a deep lake.

l: the pool, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The pool, a body of water inside the cavern under the sea, is fed by and leads into the ocean; it contains fish, yields a silver-scaled fish, and releases a strange winged creature.

l: the dark hole, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: A round black opening at the cavern's rear, the dark hole is Trot and Cap'n Bill's only possible exit; fearing a worse place, they do not enter.

l: Earth, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: is_a beautiful place The Ork says that anything above ground on Earth is better than the best things underground. Trot calls Earth a beautiful place when they emerge among trees, shrubs, flowers, and green turf.

l: Ork, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Ork, personally named Flipper, is a strange, harmless, intelligent winged creature from Orkland. Neither clearly fish nor beast, it is birdlike and brilliantly plumaged, with four stork-like legs, tough-skinned inverted chopping-bowl wings, a parrot-shaped head and curved beak, scarlet crest, finger-like claws, and a mechanical, whirling propeller tail used for flight. It is about as heavy as Cap'n Bill, can carry several people, and flies when going somewhere, though walking painfully injures its feet on rocks. Water is necessary to it, yet it is a natural enemy of water and once escaped a whirlpool and cavern with mermaids' help. Flipper's central aim is to find and return to Orkland, where its family and friends live and where Orks rule living things. Restless and widely traveled, it searches the world for its home while becoming a loyal companion to Trot and Cap'n Bill. After emerging from a pool, it introduces itself, explores and guides them through a tunnel, and flies them out. It helps them cross an island and ocean, uses berries to shrink and transport them in Trot's sunbonnet, and lands with them on a mountain in an unfamiliar country. It then leads travelers, including enlarged birds, toward and beyond the sandy desert before leaving to seek Orkland, promising to return if unsuccessful. It returns from Orkland after a welcome and celebration, rescues Button-Bright, and chooses to aid the conquest of King Krewl before returning home again. Later, as an Ork leader among other Orks, it helps carry travelers over mountains into the Land of Oz, carrying Trot and departing with the other Orks after landing them.

l: the underwater journey, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: passes_through the ocean [downward and then through still, cool depths] Trot and Cap'n Bill plunge from the boat into the murky ocean depths, fall rapidly, and then descend more slowly as unseen arms seem to support them. After reaching a great depth, they are drawn upward and sideways through still water before surfacing in the cavern's pool and being cast onto its sandy beach.

l: Flipper, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: has_parent Ork [father-son relationship] Flipper is the Ork's name, given in his account of leaving home to see the world. His father warned him about dangerous Men, but Flipper's curiosity led him to travel far from Orkland and lose track of his way home.

l: Orks, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The Orks are a race of flying creatures from Orkland, a flock usually staying near their own country, with strong claws and powerful revolving tails; they are kings of the air and rule all living things in Orkland. At least fifty arrive in Jinxland as the Scarecrow faces burning, scatter the bonfire, defeat King Krewl and his soldiers, and free the Scarecrow. They search Jinxland, find Blinkie beneath bushes, and bring her to him. They help conquer Jinxland, then mostly return home after Gloria's coronation, while four carry the travelers safely to the Land of Oz.

l: Orkland, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: is_a country [the Ork's sought destination] Orkland is the Ork's own country, which it has finally found. The Ork's family and friends welcomed it with a grand celebration after its return.

l: tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The tunnel is an underground, winding passage with a large arched ceiling, though it is straight and smooth enough to walk. Beginning beyond a narrow cavern hole, it leads past a lake below a precipice and a dangerous gulf. Trot, Cap'n Bill, and the Ork travel it for hours by candlelight until it narrows, turns, and ends at a daylight-lit rocky shaft.

l: the Ork's flight, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Ork's flight uses its propeller-like tail and small wings to fly swiftly, investigate the gulf, and safely carry Cap'n Bill and Trot separately to a distant tunnel.

l: the Ork's escape from the whirlpool, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The Ork is pulled into a whirlpool, rescued by mermaids and sheltered overnight, then swims to the cavern where Trot and Cap'n Bill are staying.

l: the exploration of the tunnel, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: The exploration of the tunnel is a tough journey led by the Ork, who discovers the opening and urges Trot and Cap'n Bill to enter. He scouts ahead by flying and walking, finds a black lake and a continuing passage, and the group travels overnight through narrow, sharply turning passages until reaching the shaft.

l: shaft, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: A deep, rocky shaft rises from its bottom to daylight far above, as the Ork carries Trot and Cap'n Bill to the surface.

l: daylight, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: comes_from above [into the shaft] Daylight reaches the travelers through the top of the shaft after they make two turns in the passage. It grows brighter as the Ork flies upward and finally gives way to clear air and sunshine.

l: island (the island previously visited), The Scarecrow of Oz
s: An island, previously visited by the midgets, has forest, vines with melons, cherry trees, and wild plums. From the hill, ocean appears on three sides and beyond the forest; Trot fears imprisonment, while Cap'n Bill considers a raft or boat to leave.

l: the forest, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: A forest behind the hill, entirely of nut trees, blocks the view; Cap'n Bill and Trot walk through it to its ocean edge.

l: melons, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: provide food and water [both] Melons grow among tangled vines on the island. Cap'n Bill cuts one open, confirms that it is ripe and safe, and shares it with Trot and the Ork; many more melons are found, providing abundant food and water.

l: house, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: At the forest’s edge, Trot notices a shed-like house; Cap’n Bill agrees it is a building, and they investigate whether it is occupied.

l: Ork's flight from the shaft, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Ork's flight from the shaft carries Trot on its shoulders and Cap'n Bill holding its rear legs as its propeller tail rises through the long shaft, bumps rough walls, and lands gently in sunshine.

l: food and water, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: comes_from melons [for the explorers] The explorers find melons, cherries, wild plums, walnuts, filberts, almonds, and chestnuts. Cap'n Bill explains that melons provide both food and water, and Trot concludes that they are unlikely to starve even if the land is an island.

l: Pessim, The Scarecrow of Oz
s: Pessim is a small, bearded man who exclusively owns and calls himself king and Observer of his island. Habitually quarrelsome and fault-finding, he complains about everything he sees; neighbors brought him there for those traits.
